union.summary: Approach cannot keep whole-column/row formulas correct when the data extent SHRINKS. Because `buildDependantsMap` expands `A:A` against the *current* bounds, the dependants map only ever contains cells inside the used extent. Clearing the last populated cell in a referenced column/row (e.g. delete A3 when bounds were rows 1–3) means the changed cell is no longer a key in the map, so `=SUM(A:A)` is not queued for recalculation and shows a stale value. The design doc only reasons about the growth direction ("cells added beyond the prior extent are picked up on their own write") and never addresses removal, so the issue's "behaves as if the range covered every populated cell … matching Excel / Google Sheets" is only half satisfied.
union.evidence: memory.ts buildDependantsMap: `const bounds = this.cellIndex.bounds(); … extractReferences(expandUnboundedRanges(cell.f, bounds))`; docs/design/sheets/formula.md: "the dependants map is rebuilt on every edit, so cells added beyond the prior extent are picked up on their own write" — only covers additions.

union.summary: Unrequested, repo-wide semantics change placed at the wrong layer: blank-skipping is added to the shared `Arguments.iterate`, so it applies to EVERY function that iterates a range, not just the aggregations the issue needs. This silently changes existing bounded-range behaviour (`=AVERAGE(A1:A10)` with blanks now divides by the non-blank count) and, more worryingly, drops cells from positional consumers (lookup/index/match-style functions built on the same iterator lose row/column alignment). The issue only asked that unused cells "contribute zero / nothing" for the new unbounded shapes; scoping this to aggregation functions (or to the aggregation helper) would fit the issue, whereas mutating the generic iterator exceeds it.

union.summary: Layer/approach preference: unbounded-range resolution is done by rewriting the formula *string* and is duplicated at four call sites (calculator, MemStore.buildDependantsMap, and three loops in YorkieStore.buildDependantsMap). per_sample.evidence: Three identical `toSrefs(extractReferences(expandUnboundedRanges(cell.f, bounds)))` blocks in YorkieStore.buildDependantsMap plus the same expression in packages/sheets/src/store/memory.ts.

per_sample.summary: Approach fit: resolution is done by textually re-serializing the formula (tokenize → rewrite REFERENCE tokens → concatenate → prepend `=`) rather than by carrying bounds into evaluation. The evaluator now runs on a string that differs from the stored `cell.f`, and reassembly depends on `extractTokens` round-tripping the original text exactly (it "fills gaps with STRING tokens"), so whitespace/casing fidelity and error positions are tied to a lexer detail. A bounds-aware resolution step in the ref-resolution layer would be a more natural abstraction; flagging as a taste/level-of-abstraction concern, not a blocker.
per_sample.evidence: `let body = ''; for (const token of tokens) { ... body += token.text } return '=' + body;` in `expandUnboundedRanges`.

per_sample.summary: Clamping uses the sheet-wide used bounds rather than per-column/per-row extents, so `A:A` expands to `A1:A{globalMaxRow}` and `fetchGridByReferences` may fetch a large sparse span on big sheets; also, a whole-column formula placed inside the referenced column (e.g. `=SUM(A:A)` in A5) now falls inside its own expanded range, creating a self-reference the issue does not discuss. Both are consequences of the up-front clamping choice and deserve a note in the design doc's limitations.
per_sample.evidence: `const formula = expandUnboundedRanges(cell.f!, await sheet.getUsedBounds()); const references = extractReferences(formula); const grid = await sheet.fetchGridByReferences(references);` with bounds from `CellIndex.bounds()` (global min/max row and col).
